history.period: Built 1939 by Rai Saheb Purna Bahadur Pradhan; architect Beg Raj Sakya
history.summary: Identity CONFIRMED. CSV DEITY FLAG: the brief says 'Vishnu temple' but every consulted source states the temple is dedicated to Lord SHIVA, with the five-expression Pancha Bakram Trinetram idol near the entrance. It was built in 1939 under the patronage of Rai Saheb Purna Bahadur Pradhan, a prominent Nepalese figure who received the honorary title 'Rai Saheb' from the Viceroy of India in 1936; the pagoda-style design (inspired by Kathmandu's Pashupatinath Temple) was by Gorkha architect Beg Raj Sakya, blending Nepali and Tibetan architectural elements. FLAG (verify): darjeeling.gov.in repeats the travel-site claim that Pradhan was 'Nepal's reigning king' - unsupported and historically implausible for 1939; treat as local lore. Minor date conflict: one review source says 1936 instead of 1939. Location note: geocoded address places it on Hill Cart Road near Ghoom; travel sources describe it as just below the toy-train railway station (verify exact siting).

name: Dhirdham Temple
town_description: Darjeeling, the 'Queen of the Hills' in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, sits at about 6,700 ft in the eastern Himalayas. Founded as a British sanatorium and hill station, it is famed for its tea gardens, the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (toy train), and panoramic views of Kanchenjunga. Dhirdham Temple stands near the toy-train line on the town's southern flank with wide views of hills, valleys and Kanchenjunga behind it.

travel.airport: Bagdogra Airport ~90 km via NH 110 (per darjeeling.gov.in)
travel.railway: Just below / about 100 m from the Darjeeling (toy train) railway station (verify exact siting)
travel.road: South of Darjeeling market centre on Hill Cart Road; a few minutes from the Mall/Chowrasta
